subject: Mutual Action Plan — Velocity pilot unit-econ sanity checks
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Walsh <sarah.walsh@acmehealth.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual Action Plan - Velocity pilot unit-econ sanity checks

Hi Sarah / Tom,

Following our workshop yesterday, attaching a lightweight checklist so we can lock the MAP line items that will drive the pilot decision next month. Two things we want to validate before the pilot kickoff:

1) Unit-econ sanity (tokens / $) based on your expected traffic slices.
2) Evaluation plan that will prove quality vs cost (batching, cache hitrate, sampling).

Quick asks from your side to close assumptions:
- Sample traffic file with 1 week of real request-level rows (we can accept anonymized request ids). Ideally CSV of timestamp, request_type, avg_input_tokens, avg_output_tokens, expected qps peaks.
- Target latency SLOs (p95 / p99), and which endpoints must be < 200ms vs acceptable slower.
- Any must-keep model flavors for fidelity (e.g., redwood-rlhf-13b or similar).

On our side we will:
- Run a back-of-envelope tokens-per-dollar model with multiple batching profiles (single-request, microbatch=8, batch=32) and two cache hit scenarios (no prefix cache, 30% prefix cache).
- Provide a recommended MAP cell with a conservative tokens/$ and a best-case tokens/$ baseline for planning.
- Deliver an evaluation plan: single-run eval set (n=1k prompts), sampling across request types, and a two-week pilot where we capture unit cost and quality regressions.

I attached 'acme_velocity_map.xlsx' with a proposed gating checklist and preliminary timeline (pilot start, 2-week evaluation, decision).

Proposed timeline summary:
- 2026-09-16: kickoff + Redwood baseline run (we'll need your sample traffic by 9/13).
- 2026-09-23: first tokens/$ snapshot, batching experiments completed.
- 2026-09-30: quality evaluation and canary roll recommendation.

Can you confirm you can share the sample traffic by EOD Monday (9/13)? If not, suggest alternative date and we will rework the schedule.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
Attachment: acme_velocity_map.xlsx (Excel, 42KB)

From: Sarah Walsh <sarah.walsh@acmehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan - Velocity pilot unit-econ sanity checks

Karthik,

Thanks — this looks great and actionable. I attached an anonymized week of request-level data as 'acme_sample_traffic.csv'. It has columns: ts, endpoint, in_tokens, out_tokens, request_type. A couple of clarifications:

- Our primary endpoints for the pilot are 'note-summarize' and 'clinical-search'. Note-summarize is high QPS but short prompts; clinical-search is lower QPS but long outputs.
- Target latency for note-summarize is p95 < 150ms, p99 < 400ms. Clinical-search is softer: p95 < 500ms is OK.
- We expect occasional bursts tied to shift changes — see peak at 08:00 and 20:00 UTC in the CSV.

We don't have a firm model flavor requirement, but prefer the 13-20B class that keeps hallucination low. Open to a small canary run on a cheaper quantized variant.

Happy to hop on a 30-min sync Friday if that speeds things up.

Best,
Sarah Walsh
Head of Integrations | Acme Health
Attachment: acme_sample_traffic.csv (CSV, 125KB)

---

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sarah Walsh <sarah.walsh@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan - Velocity pilot unit-econ sanity checks

Sarah / Karthik,

Thanks for the sample CSV — good coverage. I ran a quick pass and here are the headline assumptions we plan to include in the MAP economics cell:

Assumption set A (conservative)
- Batching profile: microbatch size = 8 (typical latency-bound config).
- Cache: prefix cache hitrate = 10% (clinician repetitive prompts assumed low).
- Tokens per request: aggregated from CSV: note-summarize avg input 45 tokens / output 28 tokens; clinical-search avg input 120 tokens / output 600 tokens.
- Estimated tokens/$ (hosted SKU baseline): 0.0024 $ per 1k tokens (post-quantization discount); that yields approx 416k tokens / $1000.

Assumption set B (aggressive)
- Batching profile: batch size = 32 for non-latency-critical windows.
- Cache hitrate = 35% during steady-state daytime.
- Tokens/$ best-case = 0.0036 $ per 1k tokens (with reserved capacity + quantized kernels).

Planned outputs for the MAP cell:
- Per-endpoint tokens/day and dollars/day under both A & B.
- Latency tradeoffs: estimated p95 under each batching profile (we'll simulate with a small microbenchmark).
- Break-even analysis for moving from hosted to dedicated (RPU/week) given your projected qps.

Action items I need from Sarah / Acme to finalize the MAP numbers:
- Confirmation that anonymized CSV represents peak weeks (or whether we should scale traffic by 1.2x for expected growth).
- Any hard limits on cost per user or monthly spend cap.
- If Acme wants us to include a dedicated capacity quote in the pilot MAP cell.

I attached 'token-econ-snapshot.csv' with my quick calc (conservative and aggressive columns) and a small worksheet for the per-endpoint cost breakout.

If helpful, Grace can run the microbenchmark this afternoon to validate p95 estimates for the microbatch=8 config.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachment: token-econ-snapshot.csv (CSV, 18KB)

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan - Velocity pilot unit-econ sanity checks

Perfect — this is exactly the granularity we wanted. Two quick next steps:
1) Sarah: if you can confirm whether that week is representative (or say go ahead to scale traffic by 1.2x), we'll lock the MAP economics cell by EOD Monday 9/13.
2) Ben / Grace: please run the microbenchmark on the microbatch=8 and batch=32 configs and upload p95/p99 sims to the Drive folder linked in the MAP.

I'll schedule a 30-minute sync Friday 9/11 at 10am PT to walk through the conservative vs aggressive MAP rows and finalize the pilot gating criteria. Invite sent.
